title: A father speaks to his son about the resurrection
summary: A speaker addresses his son’s concern about the resurrection, teaches that it follows the coming of Christ, and says he has diligently inquired of God about it.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker addresses his son and says he perceives that his son is worried about the resurrection of the dead.
The speaker says that resurrection follows the coming of Christ and that Christ brings about the resurrection of the dead.
The speaker says he has diligently inquired of God concerning the resurrection.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker can be shown addressing his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s and son’s appearances, clothing, ages, postures, and precise setting are not stated.

spoken_dialogue.text: Now my son, here is somewhat more I would say unto thee; for I perceive that thy mind is worried concerning the resurrection of the dead.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unnamed speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, my son, the resurrection is not yet.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unnamed speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Neither the speaker nor his son is named in the supplied verse text. The resurrection and Christ’s coming are discussed, not narrated as occurring here.

title: The appointed time
summary: Alma teaches that all will come forth from the dead at a time appointed by God, and that a space lies between death and resurrection.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says an appointed time will come when all shall come forth from the dead, and only God knows when.
Alma says it does not matter whether there is one appointed time or more than one; all shall rise from the dead.
Alma says there must be a space between death and resurrection.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown continuing his address to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of any dead people, the appointed time, and the setting are unspecified.

narration.text: there is a time appointed that all shall come forth from the dead.
there must needs be a space betwixt the time of death and the time of the resurrection.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These statements are teachings, not depictions of a resurrection event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not visualize a specific resurrection time or portray the dead rising in this scene.

title: The question between death and resurrection
summary: Alma asks what becomes of souls between death and resurrection and says he has diligently inquired of the Lord about this interval.

explicit_facts.text: Alma asks what becomes of the souls of men between death and the appointed resurrection.
Alma says all do not die at once and that time is measured unto men.
Alma says there is a space between death and resurrection, and that he diligently inquired of the Lord about the souls' state during it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown addressing his son while explaining his inquiry.
unspecified_visual_details: No location, visible souls, or means of measuring time is described.

this is the thing of which I do know.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma's question and explanation are teaching, not a narrated event involving visible souls.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a clock, timeline, or souls in a particular place.

title: The souls' state made known
summary: Alma says an angel made known to him that departed spirits are taken home to God; righteous spirits are received into paradise, a state of happiness, rest, and peace.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says that when all rise, they will know God knows all appointed times.
Alma says an angel made known that the spirits of all people, good or evil, are taken home to God after departing their mortal bodies.
Alma says righteous spirits are received into paradise, a state of happiness, rest, and peace, free from troubles, care, and sorrow.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma can be shown recounting what an angel made known; the angel need not be present in the teaching moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel's appearance, any vision setting, God's appearance, and paradise's visual appearance are not specified.

title: The wicked in darkness
summary: Alma teaches that the wicked are cast into outer darkness, where there is weeping, wailing, and gnashing of teeth, and remain in darkness until resurrection.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the wicked chose evil works, are cast into outer darkness, and experience weeping, wailing, and gnashing of teeth.
Alma says the wicked remain in darkness, awaiting the fiery indignation of God's wrath, until resurrection.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma can be shown teaching his son; the descriptions of darkness and misery are theological teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of outer darkness, the wicked spirits, and any literal fire is not specified.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show literal flames, a devil figure, or graphic torment.

title: What is called the first resurrection
summary: Alma distinguishes the soul's assignment to happiness or misery from the first resurrection, which he explains as the reuniting of soul and body from Adam's days down to Christ's resurrection.

explicit_facts.text: Alma acknowledges that the soul's raising and assignment to happiness or misery may be termed a resurrection by some.
Alma cites the first resurrection as pertaining to those down to the resurrection of Christ.
Alma rejects the idea that this first resurrection means the soul's assignment to happiness or misery, and says it means the reuniting of soul and body from Adam's days down to Christ's resurrection.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown teaching without visualizing the historical figures or the resurrection.
unspecified_visual_details: No scene of Adam, Christ, or any soul-body reunion is described here.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma is clarifying the meaning of a doctrinal term.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the first resurrection as a present event or show Adam or Christ physically present.

title: The appointed reunion and judgment
summary: Alma says those who die before Christ's resurrection will come forth before those who die afterward. He offers his opinion about the righteous' reunion, then teaches that all will be reunited and stand before God to be judged.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says those previously discussed all come forth before those who die after Christ's resurrection, without specifying whether all are reunited at once.
Alma gives his opinion that the righteous are reunited at Christ's resurrection and ascension into heaven, while qualifying that he does not say whether it occurs then or later.
Alma says the dead will be reunited, both soul and body, stand before God, and be judged according to their works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma can be shown presenting his teaching; judgment and resurrection are not occurring in the present teaching moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise order and timing, God's visible appearance, and any judgment scene details are not specified.

title: Restoration

explicit_facts.text: Alma says restoration brings about what the prophets spoke.
Alma says the soul and body, every limb and joint, and every hair will be restored to the proper and perfect frame.

title: The outcomes of righteousness and wickedness
summary: Alma teaches that the righteous will shine forth in the kingdom of God, while the wicked are cast out to partake of the fruits of their evil works.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the righteous will shine forth in the kingdom of God.
Alma says an awful death comes upon the wicked, who are unclean and cannot inherit God's kingdom; they are cast out to partake of the fruits of their evil works.
